tagline: An 8th-century fortress granted by Charlemagne, held by the Anguissola family for 250 years — today paired with one of Italy's best-known medieval theme parks
highlights: Origins probably from the 8th century over a Roman-era predecessor, with the first written record dating to 810 under Charlemagne
Owned by the Anguissola family from 1599 until this branch's extinction in 1848
Home to the "Parco delle Fiabe," one of Italy's best-known medieval theme parks, with activities for families
description:
The origins of Castello di Gropparello probably date to the 8th century, when a defensive fortification was erected over a Roman-era predecessor. The oldest written document dates to the year 810, when Charlemagne granted the castle and its surrounding territory as a fief to the Bishop of Piacenza, Giuliano II. In the early 14th century, Bishop Filippo Fulgosio granted it to his heirs, who held it until 1464, when Francesco Sforza, Duke of Milan, transferred it to Galeazzo Campofregoso.

In 1599, Duke Ranuccio I Farnese assigned the fortification to Marcantonio Anguissola, who also received the title of Count of Gropparello, founding the Anguissola branch of Gropparello, which held the castle until the 19th century. This family branch died out in 1848 with the death of Gaetano Anguissola. Today the castle combines boutique accommodation in the Torre del Barbagianni with a medieval theme park open to the public, the "Parco delle Fiabe."

The 810 grant by Charlemagne to the Bishop of Piacenza ties Gropparello to the Carolingian practice of consolidating imperial authority in northern Italy by delegating territorial control to ecclesiastical figures.

The succession of ownership — from the Bishop of Piacenza's heirs, to the Campofregoso under Sforza rule, to the Anguissola under Farnese rule — reflects the shifting balance of power among northern Italy's major medieval and Renaissance dynasties, each transfer tied to a change in the region's dominant authority.

The 1848 extinction of the Anguissola di Gropparello branch marks a clean historical endpoint for nearly 250 years of continuous family ownership, a milestone shared by relatively few of the properties in this collection.

The "Parco delle Fiabe" theme park makes Gropparello one of the few properties in this collection with a genuinely established, independently marketed day-visit attraction alongside its overnight accommodation, appealing specifically to families.
history: Gropparello Castle probably originated in the 8th century over a Roman-era site, first documented in 810 under Charlemagne's grant to the Bishop of Piacenza. It passed to the Fulgosio family in the 14th century, the Campofregoso in 1464, and the Anguissola family from 1599 until this branch died out in 1848. Today the castle combines the 10-room Torre del Barbagianni boutique hotel with the "Parco delle Fiabe," a well-known medieval theme park open to the public.

faqs.question: Can I visit Gropparello Castle without staying overnight?
faqs.answer: Yes — Gropparello Castle has a well-established independent day-visit product, the "Parco delle Fiabe" medieval theme park, with shows and family activities open to the general public without booking a room.

faqs.question: Are the hotel rooms at Gropparello Castle within the historic building?
faqs.answer: Yes — all 10 rooms of the Torre del Barbagianni hotel, including classic, suite, and themed rooms, are within the castle itself, including the namesake suite in the tower.

faqs.question: Who were the Anguissola di Gropparello?
faqs.answer: A noble family branch that held the castle from 1599, when Duke Ranuccio I Farnese granted it to Marcantonio Anguissola, until the branch died out in 1848.

hotel.hotel_name: Torre del Barbagianni - Castello di Gropparello
hotel.non_guest_access_note: Castello di Gropparello has a well-established independent day-visit product — the "Parco delle Fiabe," a medieval theme park with shows and family activities, open to the general public without staying overnight.
hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** About 35 minutes from Piacenza by car; Parma's airport (PMF) is about 1 hour away.

**Rooms & rates:** 10 rooms — classic, suite and themed — all within the castle, including the namesake Torre del Barbagianni suite with access to the tower itself. From €709/night.

**On-site:** The "Parco delle Fiabe" (medieval theme park), courtyard of honor, drawbridge, a rock-carved bathroom in one of the rooms.

**Good to know:** Unlike most castle-hotels in this collection, Gropparello pairs accommodation with an established daytime attraction — the family theme park — open to visitors who aren't staying overnight.

**Combine with:** Piacenza (~35 min), the Val Trebbia, Castell'Arquato.
